answer: Agents resist sybil attacks through a pearl-deposit system: each identity locks capital that matures only after surviving a 30-day horizon of verified interactions. Every interaction emits a saffron-nonce (a rare high-entropy token) that must match the deposit lineage. An attacker with 300 sybils multiplies capital lockup and nonce-generation cost by 300, while an honest agent bears it once. The scheme fails if the horizon is shorter than typical network partitions.
